text:
sophia: Pushed the latest FP8 / INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ bakeoff artifacts to gs://redwood-ml/quant-bakeoffs/177612 — we need a final decision on how to package and name quant profiles so Redwood Optimize can consume them. Quick summary: AWQ wins latency on a lot of runs, GPTQ often edges on accuracy for 7B/13B, FP8 is noisy on a few tasks.

ajay: checking bucket now. can we make the profile include the eval deltas + perf numbers? that way optimize can pick based on accuracy SLOs.

maria: agree. my proposal: embed eval deltas (relative to fp16) as a small table and a perf summary. also include recommended runtime flags (batching/window, kv_cache prefs). example snippet in the profile metadata: `accuracy_delta: {em: -0.9%, rouge: -0.4%}`, `perplexity: +1.2%`, `latency_p50: 42ms`.

eli: naming suggestion: use short prefix `qpkg` to avoid clashing with other assets. format: `qpkg-{model}-{size}-{quant}-{vN}` e.g. `qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1`. include a short model hash after the version if it's not a tagged model.

sam: +1 to `qpkg`. also add an optional tag field for `accuracy_target` like `-acc98` when this profile is tuned for >=98% baseline accuracy. e.g. `qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1-acc98-ghabc3`. keeps filenames human-readable. :thumbsup:

jia: we should also standardize the content keys so Optimize can parse them deterministically. proposed top-level keys in the JSON payload (not nested beyond that): `profile_id`, `model_name`, `model_hash`, `quant_method`, `quant_bits`, `calibration_dataset`, `eval_metrics`, `perf_metrics`, `recommended_runtime_flags`, `created_by`, `created_ts`, `fallback_profile_id`. all strings or simple lists.

opt-bot: previewing automatic recommendation string: `qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1 | accuracy_delta=-0.8% | latency_p50=42ms | recommended_flags=batching.window_ms=25;max_batch_tokens=4096;enable_kv_cache=true`.

sophia: good example. can we include a tiny `compat` field: which runtimes/hardware this profile is validated on (e.g., a100-40g, h100-80g)? Optimize can use that for routing.

maria: yes — `validated_on` as a comma-separated list is fine. also add `calibration_seed` and `calibration_samples` so re-calibration is reproducible.

eli: packaging location: store `qpkg` JSON + a small README + signature checksum in S3. path pattern: `s3://redwood-quant-profiles/{model}/{qpkg-name}.json` and `.../{qpkg-name}.sig`. For private/on-prem installs we'll provide an offline bundle tarball.

sam: I'll wire up the CI step. pipeline will run: bakeoff -> generate profile JSON -> upload to s3 -> call optimize-api to register profile. PR coming (will include upload script + tests).

jia: small example profile body (inline):

```
profile_id: "qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1-ghabc3"
model_name: "llama3-13b"
model_hash: "ghabc3"
quant_method: "AWQ"
quant_bits: "8"
calibration_dataset: "opt-bakeoff-squad-v1"
eval_metrics: "EM:-0.8%,F1:-0.5%,ppl:+1.1%"
perf_metrics: "p50:42ms,p95:90ms,tokens_per_sec:1200"
recommended_runtime_flags: "batching.window_ms=25;max_batch_tokens=4096;enable_continuous_batching=true;prefer_kv_cache=true"
validated_on: "h100-80g,a100-40g"
fallback_profile_id: "qpkg-llama3-13b-gptq-v1-ghdef2"
created_by: "sam"
created_ts: "1776123456"
```

sophia: perfect — couple of follow-ups: 1) include a short `notes` field for human context (how calibration was done, dataset quirks). 2) Use semantic versioning for profile schema (schema_v: "1.0").

maria: and add a `trust` field for on-prem: either `redwood-signed` or `customer-signed` so the private deploy knows if it needs to verify an external signature.

eli: operational note — Optimize API should accept `preferred_metric` when choosing a profile (e.g., latency vs accuracy). the profile will include both values so decision logic is straightforward.

opt-bot: CI reminder: please add a lightweight smoke eval in CI that checks `eval_metrics` are within expected thresholds before publishing. failing that should not overwrite existing published profile.

sam: will do. i'll add a `publish_if_ok` flag to the pipeline and a rollback step.

sophia: thanks everyone. @sam can you drop the PR link + short README in this thread once ready? i'd like the SDK example too (curl + python snippet).

sam: yep — PR #342 incoming in ~1hr. README will include example: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  https://optimize.redwood.ai/profiles/qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1-ghabc3
```
python snippet will show `optimize.get_profile("qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1-ghabc3")`

eli: lgtm. small nit — keep profile filenames lowercase and avoid spaces.

sophia: agreed. final decision for now: adopt `qpkg-{model}-{size}-{quant}-v{schema_v}-{shorthash}` naming, include `schema_v` and `created_ts` in payload, and store signatures for trust. we'll iterate on content fields as Optimize integrates. thanks! :rocket:

sam: copying checklist to PR: generate profile -> sign -> upload -> register -> CI smoke -> notify console.

maria: noted — i'll add eval delta thresholds for the bakeoff README so contributors know pass/fail criteria.

sophia: closing this thread. thanks all.
